si.t: Phase 1 working input for the website content writer and designer. Website positioning becomes the master source for future marketing, social media, articles, blogs, brochures, emails and other brand communication. This should evolve into a living reference for what Niche Global is about.

Niche Global is developing an overseas education and global career-pathway proposition focused primarily on people from Kerala. “Global Career Company” remains a working positioning and should be legally/regulatorily validated before formal use.
Profile first. Career outcome first. Pathway second. Understand the individual before recommending a destination or route.
USA | UK | Australia | France | South Korea
Real First. AI Enhanced. Never Generic.
Don't tell people what Niche Global isn't. Show them what Niche Global is.
Sell the career and life outcome — not the visa, course or pathway.
Trust should come from how Niche Global operates, not from exaggerated advertising claims.

Primary conversion: Find My Pathway / Check My Profile. Contextual exploration: Explore [Country], Explore Pathways, Our Story. High-intent conversation: Talk to Us / equivalent. Do not force a CTA into every section.

Current activities should be framed around services Niche Global is legally permitted to provide. Direct overseas recruitment, employment placement, work-visa claims, guarantees, partner terminology and outcome claims require validation before publication.

No merged cells. Repeat parent section names for every component/row so sorting and filtering remain functional. Yellow cells are intended for designer links; green cells for final content-writer copy.
Homepage only for now. Inner pages to be developed later if required.

First impression of Niche Global. Establish that the brand helps people explore realistic pathways to build a career and potentially a life internationally. Focus on the destination and career outcome, not the mechanism used to get there.

Headline is fixed: “Life Beyond Borders.” Supporting copy should be only 1–2 short lines. Communicate that Niche Global helps identify suitable international career pathways based on profile, education, experience, skills, career goals and ambitions. Do not explain visas, programs, fees or processes. Career/life outcome first; pathway second.

USA-led opening visual, preferably San Francisco / Silicon Valley / Bay Area. Premium, wide international career/lifestyle image with subtle blur/dark treatment. Avoid graduation caps, campuses, passports, visa stamps, airplanes, suitcases, excessive flags and typical overseas-education imagery.
Primary CTA: Find My Pathway / Discover My Pathway / Explore My Options. Final wording to be recommended by content writer.
Hero Scroll 2 — Your Profile Comes First
Communicate that Niche Global begins with the individual rather than starting with a country, course, visa or predefined program.
Create a short headline and maximum 1–2 lines around understanding the person’s education, experience, skills, profile and ambitions first. Keep it personalized and confident.
Use the real Niche Global/Niche office in Kochi. Prefer an authentic consultation/discussion between team and candidate. Enhance lighting/cleanliness if needed while keeping the office recognizable.
Contextual CTA optional. Do not force a CTA if it disrupts the hero flow.
Hero Scroll 3 — Different People, Different Pathways
Show that there is no single route to an international career. The appropriate route depends on the individual profile and destination.
Short headline + maximum 1–2 lines. Communicate the concept of multiple possible pathways without turning the hero into a visa/program list or implying universal eligibility.
Sophisticated multiple-pathway/global-opportunity visual or authentic consultation imagery. Avoid cliché forked-road graphics and generic visa imagery.
Contextual CTA optional; primary website CTA remains Find My Pathway.

Establish a key Niche Global philosophy: simply going abroad is not the success metric. The pathway should make sense for employability, international experience, earning potential and longer-term career direction.
Short headline + maximum 1–2 lines. Focus on outcome and career progression. Avoid guarantees or promises of jobs, visas, settlement or income.
Authentic international workplace/career imagery; preferably real candidate/program outcome imagery as the asset library grows.
Contextual CTA optional. Keep the hero uncluttered.

Establish who Niche Global is, where it comes from and why it exists. Define Niche Global on its own terms rather than comparing it with overseas education consultancies, recruitment agencies or visa companies.

Communicate: profile-first approach; person → career → destination → pathway; U.S. roots, Kochi presence, Kerala focus; origin from Niche Techies’ U.S. technology talent/staff-augmentation background. Keep to section label + headline + approx. 60–80 words + optional credibility statement. Do not explain what Niche Global is 'not'.
Use real Kochi office/team imagery, ideally an authentic consultation or discussion. Real first, AI enhanced, never generic. Office should remain recognizable.
Exploration CTA: Our Story / Learn More About Niche Global, if a dedicated About page exists. Otherwise no CTA.
Explain how Niche Global thinks before introducing individual programs. Turn the brand promise into a simple methodology.

Guide content around: Understand Your Profile → Define Career Direction → Identify Markets → Evaluate Pathways → Recommend Next Steps. Exact number/names can be refined. Section should answer “What happens when I come to Niche Global?” without visa, fee, university or program detail. Use section label + headline + short intro + one short line per step.
Clean process visualization/cards/timeline rather than another large photo. Could visually resemble a profile-matching process without looking overly technical or AI-heavy.
Start My Profile Evaluation / Find My Pathway. CTA should lead toward the profile evaluation experience.
Introduce USA as one of a deliberately selected set of international career markets. Country is a career market, not a travel/study destination.

Country name + short headline + 1–2 line career-oriented statement + 2–3 relevant career/pathway areas if appropriate + Explore USA CTA. Direction: technology, professional careers, employer ecosystem and multiple profile-dependent pathways. Do not explain visas/fees/program details here.
One-country-at-a-time full-width carousel. San Francisco / Silicon Valley / modern professional environment. Premium, consistent treatment across all destination slides.
Present UK as a selected career market with specific relevance to the profiles/pathways Niche Global serves.

Country name + short headline + 1–2 lines + 2–3 relevant areas if appropriate. Direction: healthcare and other identified professional career opportunities. Avoid generic 'dream destination' language.
London or recognizable modern professional environment; avoid overly tourist-heavy Big Ben/red-bus treatment.
Present Australia as a selected career market based on relevant professional/skilled pathways.
Country name + short headline + 1–2 lines + 2–3 relevant areas. Direction: healthcare and selected skilled/professional career opportunities. Eligibility depends on profile.
Sydney/Melbourne modern career/lifestyle imagery rather than beach/tourism imagery.
Present France as a selected market with specific career-pathway relevance.
Country name + short headline + 1–2 lines + 2–3 relevant areas. Direction: hospitality, culinary and international hotel career pathways. Keep homepage high-level.
Premium France imagery connected to the sectors actually served, especially hospitality; not necessarily generic Paris tourism.
Present South Korea as a selected market for specialized career/training opportunities.
Country name + short headline + 1–2 lines + 2–3 relevant areas. Direction: selected specialized career, training and industry-specific pathways. Avoid overclaiming.
Modern Seoul/contemporary professional environment. Avoid making the visual entirely K-pop/entertainment focused.
Introduce types of legitimate international career pathways without becoming a visa catalogue. Country = where; pathway = how.

Create consumer-friendly pathway name + one concise description focused on what the pathway is designed to accomplish. Employment/employer sponsorship may form part of the route where legally and factually applicable. Do not imply availability to everyone.
Clean pathway card/tile with simple visual/icon. Consistent with other pathway cards.
Explore Pathways / Learn More, only if a destination page exists.
Show education as one possible strategic pathway toward a career outcome, not the defining Niche Global category.
Consumer-friendly name + one concise description. Education can be used strategically where it creates access to relevant international experience/post-study career possibilities. Avoid guarantees.
Introduce structured international internship experience as one possible pathway.
Consumer-friendly name + concise description around building international experience/profile and possible subsequent career opportunities. Do not promise conversion to employment.
Introduce international training, professional development and eligible exchange routes.
Consumer-friendly name + concise description. Keep technical visa terminology out of homepage copy unless necessary.
Allow for profile-specific routes for experienced, skilled or otherwise qualifying professionals.
Consumer-friendly name + concise description. Reinforce that eligibility and appropriate route depend on individual profile, destination and applicable requirements.

Answer why a visitor should trust Niche Global with an important international career decision. Build credibility through how the company operates, where it comes from and how recommendations are made.

Build around approx. five reasons: U.S. Roots/Kerala Focus; Profile Before Pathway; Career Outcome in Mind; Selected Markets, Not Everything Everywhere; International Ecosystem where factually supportable. Use section label + headline + 2–3 line intro + 4–6 short reason statements. Avoid No.1, best, guaranteed job/visa, 100% success or unsupported claims.

Strongly authentic. Use real Kochi office, team, candidate consultations, partner meetings and international program/interaction imagery. Could use clean 3–5 image collage. AI may enhance genuine assets but should not invent the reality.
High-intent conversation CTA. Direction: Talk to Us / Meet Our Team / Talk to a Career Advisor. Final terminology to be legally/brand validated.

Show that Niche Global operates through a growing international ecosystem of institutions, training organizations, employers, hotel groups, industry partners and strategic relationships where applicable.

Section label + headline + approx. 2 lines. Use precise relationship terminology: Partner / Institution / Training Provider / Employer Network / Hotel Network / Strategic Relationship. Do not call every organization a partner without verification or permission.

Logo-led, clean and premium. Horizontal logo carousel, potentially grouped by country. Use only verified logos/relationships and confirm public display permission. Optional authentic partner/program image.
No CTA by default. Explore Our Network only if a dedicated network page is created.
Create verified partner/network master list including organization, country, relationship type, relevant pathway, logo permission, website and public-display status.
Humanize the proposition through authentic candidate journeys. Show starting point → pathway → destination → outcome. Candidate is the hero, not Niche Global.

For each story: candidate name; starting profile; country/pathway; 2–4 line journey summary; current outcome where verifiable; optional short quote. Avoid generic praise/testimonials. Exact story must be real and documented.
Real candidate photos/videos only. Prioritize departure, training, internship/workplace and destination assets. No AI-generated people. One featured journey at a time in horizontal scroll.
Build candidate story asset library: before profile, pathway, country, photos, videos, current status, outcome, testimonial, publication permission.
Second authentic journey; prioritize diversity of profile/country/pathway.
Same content structure as 08A. Select a genuinely strong, documented story.
Third authentic journey. Three strong stories are the minimum recommended for launch.
Same content structure as 08A. Do not create filler stories simply to reach the target.
Additional featured journey toward target of six.
Same content structure; prioritize diversity of country/career area/pathway.
Sixth featured journey. Homepage target is six; launch minimum is three strong stories.
Turn the Profile First philosophy into an interactive experience. Help visitors explore what may fit without requiring them to understand countries, visas or programs first.
Provide section headline + very short introduction. Message should invite the visitor to tell Niche Global where they are today. Avoid promising automated eligibility.
Conversational, mobile-first interactive UI. One simple question at a time. Tap whenever possible; type only when necessary.
Primary: Check My Profile. Secondary/escape path: Talk to Us.
If development threatens launch timing, Phase 1 fallback is profile cards + simple evaluation/contact form.
Create clear question wording and predefined answers: Plus Two / Diploma / Bachelor's / Master's / Other. Other can open free-text input.
Large tap-friendly answer buttons/cards; no keyboard unless Other is selected.
Continue automatically after selection; persistent subtle Talk to Us option.
Understand where the visitor is in the career journey.
Question + predefined answers such as Student / Fresher / 1–3 Years / 3–7 Years / 7+ Years / Other.
Continue; allow Not Sure/Other where useful.
Capture broad career/industry area for routing and qualification.
Question + predefined answers such as Technology / Healthcare / Hospitality / Business / Engineering / Finance / Other. Categories can be refined based on actual offerings.
Tap-first category cards; Other opens free text.
Understand what the visitor is trying to achieve rather than assuming the solution.
Question + answers such as Work Abroad / Build an International Career / International Experience / Career Change / Not Sure Yet. Final language to be refined by content writer.
Capture destination preference without forcing the visitor to choose a solution.
USA / UK / Australia / France / South Korea / I'm Open. 'I'm Open' is important and should be clearly visible.
Country options as clean cards/buttons; avoid making this look like a country catalogue.
Collect contact details after the visitor has invested in the matcher, rather than at the beginning.
Provide wording around having a better picture of the profile and inviting the visitor to continue. Fields: Name, WhatsApp/Phone, Email. Include privacy/consent language.
Clean, short form at the end of the interactive sequence.
Get My Profile Evaluated / equivalent. Also retain Talk to Us path.
Locked / Phase 1 Target; Full logic may be Phase 2
Give useful direction without making automated eligibility promises.

Use careful language such as 'Your profile may be worth exploring for…' or 'Potential areas to evaluate.' Never 'Congratulations, you qualify.' Results can show markets/pathways as Worth Exploring / Potential Match / Requires Further Evaluation. Human review should remain central.
Personalized result cards/summary. Keep transparent that this is preliminary and subject to evaluation.
Get My Profile Evaluated / Talk to Our Team
Phase 2 can add full matching logic, CRM integration, lead scoring and saved profiles.
Explain what happens after someone engages with Niche Global. Distinct from Section 03: this is the customer journey, not the pathway-selection methodology.

Guide around: Profile Evaluation → Opportunity & Pathway Discussion → Pathway Selection → Preparation & Processing → International Transition → Career Progression. Validate exact operational steps. Use section label + headline + 1–2 line intro + step name + one short explanation each. Avoid operational checklists/payment details.
Clean horizontal timeline on desktop and vertical timeline on mobile. Process should be the visual hero. Real candidate imagery can appear subtly but should not distract.
Start With My Profile / Start My Evaluation. Can link back to Section 09 matcher.
Validate the actual operational process before final copy.
Reserved for genuine visitor concerns once the rest of the website and business positioning are clearer.
Do not draft generic FAQs yet. Build questions later from real candidate concerns, sales conversations, legal/compliance needs and website user behavior.
Placeholder only. Final visual format to be decided after FAQ scope is defined.
Get in Touch / Start Your Journey
Provide a conventional, low-friction lead-capture path for visitors who do not want to use the interactive profile matcher. Complement, not replace, the matcher and WhatsApp/talk option.

Provide headline + 1–2 line supporting message + field labels + placeholder text where needed + CTA + submission confirmation + consent/privacy language. Suggested fields: Full Name*, Phone/WhatsApp*, Email, Current Qualification*, Current Career Status*, Interested Country (USA/UK/Australia/France/South Korea/Not Sure Yet), optional Message. Do not collect detailed age/passport/marks/salary/budget data here.

Two-column layout: left = authentic Kochi office/candidate consultation image and short message; right = clean static form. Mobile stacks content then form. Keep visually simple and conversion-focused.
Static form CTA direction: Request a Callback / Talk to Niche Global / Submit — final wording by content writer. Keep WhatsApp/talk option available as lowest-friction path.
